title: How to use Blender to create fashion animation?
content:
Hey everyone! 🌟 I'm Phidias, a 3D Pattern Designer using CLO3D, and I'm super excited to dive into the world of 3D pattern design!

I was wondering if anyone could suggest some great tutorials on using Blender for fashion. I'm eager to learn how to use Blender! 🤓🙏🏻

If you have any tips on starting with 3D software or even AI, I’d appreciate it!

Thanks a million, and I can't wait to hear your suggestions! 😊

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/260805a565254731958da26c8018db45/images/74c9153712b74e378ee21a6d180aa1f51000140391.jpg)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: I'm also trying to learn Blender, but I don't have any guidelines. It's not as easy as CLO 3D.
Reply 1: Yes, I agree. There are many shortcuts to remember. It will be easier to use.

Comment 3: Blender donut by blender guru to get your feet wet and get a feel for the workflow, from modelling to texturing to rendering.
Reply 1: Thank you so much guys! You all are the best!

Comment 4: Hello! First, you can start by learning the basic operations of Blender, then look at what effects you want to achieve and search for keywords to learn and apply to your project, such as software name + operational requirements + scene building, lighting, character animation, etc. You can also create characters or accessories in Blender and import them back to CLO3D. This will be a challenging and exciting endeavor!
Reply 1: Thank you so much guys! You all are the best!
content_description: A community-driven page where 3D pattern designer Phidias seeks beginner-friendly Blender tutorials and tips on 3D software and AI for fashion design.

title: Troubleshooting: Auto Fitting and Arrangement Points
content:
# Are you getting these alerts when importing your custom avatar?

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/12dc15957be44852b7ec66959a774353/images/596ac93da385443299075c073c4fbd0eimage.png)

**_"Arrangement points were not fitted to the avatar. The avatar must be in a T-pose or A-pose."_**

_Or  
"_**_Fitting Suit cannot be created._**_The avatar must be in a T-Pose or A-pose"_

There can be a lot of reasons that you might see these errors. First, always best check the "Best Practice Checklist" below and see if it matches what you have so far!

**Best Practice Checklist for Importing Avatars**

  * Avatar is 1 mesh body

  * Avatar has closed geometry (no holes)

  * Avatar is 1,200-2,000 millimeters tall

  * Avatar is in an A-Pose

  * Avatar has 2 arms, 2 legs, 1 head

  * Importing a OBJ or FBX file type

  * Correct normal direction (normals facing outward)




After double checking (or not, it will be covered in the flowchart) we can move onto the flow chart.

![](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202502/12dc15957be44852b7ec66959a774353/images/c39f3d2fe4514096ad22d1d1f3266a9dimage.png)

If you are stuck or end up in the "contact support" portion. Make sure to contact the software support team of the software you are using: 

  * For Marvelous Designer: <https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact>

  * For CLO: [https://www.clo3d.com/en/support](https://www.clo3d.com/en/support)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Thank you! This is super helpful!
content_description: This page helps users troubleshoot common errors when importing custom avatars by providing best practices and a step-by-step flowchart.
